analysis.headline: Relay-heavy release: the only KEV is inherited Linux kernel code
summary: Fourteen of the 22 fixes are Reyrolle 7SR5 protection relays, including the release's worst-scored network flaw (CVE-2026-62645, 9.8, auth bypass via computable session IDs). The only KEV entry, CVE-2026-31431, is not a Siemens-authored defect at all: it is a Linux kernel algif_aead bug carried inside SIPLUS/SIMATIC images, and it carries EPSS 1.00. The third critical, CVE-2026-50093 (Siveillance OIS arbitrary file upload to root), is the shortest path from a web request to host compromise in the bundle.

Nine items are tagged automatable and the exploitable surface is concentrated in product web front ends, not in the kernel CVE the coverage clustered around. Our own newsroom covered four CVEs — the KEV, the two Siemens AV advisories, and the Desigo CC graphics-script bug — while skipping the 9.8 relay auth bypass, the unauthenticated directory traversal in SIMOVE/SIPLANT, and the Mendix SAML signature-validation failure. Nothing here is flagged exploited or pre-disclosure, so this is a patch-cadence release, not an incident.

themes.title: Reyrolle 7SR5 is the release, not a footnote
themes.detail: One product line accounts for 14 of 22 CVEs and covers every failure mode that matters on a substation relay: authentication bypass through computable session IDs, low-entropy session tokens, RBAC checks bypassed by request manipulation, pre-auth out-of-bounds write and resource exhaustion that force reboots, plus five 2024-vintage Cesanta Mongoose v7.14 web-server bugs still shipping in firmware.

themes.title: Inherited components set the top of the scoreboard
themes.detail: The highest-EPSS items are not Siemens code: a Linux kernel AEAD revert (KEV, EPSS 1.00), a Keycloak reset-credentials flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker force another user's password reset, a Mendix SAML module that does not validate response signatures, and Mongoose 7.14. This is upstream debt re-shipped inside OT firmware and appliance images, so Siemens advisory IDs are the only patch signal an admin gets.

themes.title: Unauthenticated file handling on exposed web interfaces
themes.detail: Directory traversal in the SIMOVE/SIPLANT embedded HTTP server reads arbitrary files with no credentials; Siveillance OIS accepts arbitrary uploads and lands root; Desigo CC executes attacker script embedded in a graphics document. Descriptions differ, exposure does not: anything reachable from an engineering VLAN is a file-write or code-execution primitive.

themes.title: The tail is physical-access and firmware-reversing filler
themes.detail: Three Reyrolle items require a thumb on the device (boot-key maintenance mode that runs unsigned code, proprietary-port memory corruption in firmware-update mode) or only ease reverse engineering of publicly downloadable firmware. They are real but do not change network exposure, and they inflate the headline count of a 22-CVE release whose actionable set is closer to eight.

analysis.data_vs_prose: The aggregates contradict themselves and the row data: epss_ge_10 (2) cannot be smaller than epss_ge_50 (4), and remote_unauth is 0 while at least six descriptions state plainly that an unauthenticated remote attacker can act (CVE-2026-62645, -67367, -62648, -62649, -62646, -50093). KEV=1 with exploited=0 and disclosed=0 is also unresolved — treat KEV as the exploitation signal. Trust the per-row EPSS values (1.00, 0.94, 0.66, 0.51) and the CVSS column over the band counts. What the headlines miss is structural: they lead with the kernel KEV and advisory stubs, so the relay cluster, the SIMOVE traversal, and the Mendix SAML signature gap got no coverage at all, while Desigo CC (40.8) was covered ahead of three higher-scored CVEs.

watchlist.why: Only KEV entry and EPSS 1.00; kernel-level privilege path in SIPLUS/SIMATIC images, but remediation ships only with Siemens firmware, so confirm which images carry the affected kernel.
9.8, computable current and past session IDs allow auth bypass on Reyrolle 7SR5 — highest-impact network flaw in the release and uncovered by us.
9.1 automatable Keycloak reset-credentials abuse; forces password resets for arbitrary users without interaction, so it is an account-takeover chain in Industrial Edge Management.
9.0 arbitrary upload in Siveillance OIS web module ending in host root — full OIS environment compromise from the app tier.
8.6 unauthenticated directory traversal reading arbitrary OS files from SIMOVE/SIPLANT; no credentials needed, so it is also a reconnaissance and credential-harvesting primitive.
8.7 unvalidated SAML response signature in the Mendix module — session hijack wherever SSO is configured that way; check module version before assuming IdP-side mitigations hold.
8.8 RBAC bypass by request manipulation; low-privileged authenticated escalation that pairs with the session-prediction bugs on the same relays.
7.4 session identifiers generated without a TRNG yield predictable values; combined with CVE-2026-62645/-62646 it makes brute-force bypass practical rather than theoretical.

analysis.patch_note: Reyrolle 7SR5 first — highest CVE density, both non-kernel criticals of the OT side, and pre-auth DoS that takes protection functions offline; schedule an outage since reboot is the failure mode. Then Siveillance Control OIS (upload to root) and SIMOVE/SIPLANT (unauth file read) as internet/engineering-VLAN exposures, then Industrial Edge Management for the Keycloak component and the Mendix SAML module, then Desigo CC and WTV676/WTV776, with Teamcenter trailing. CVE-2026-31431 is patched by the SIMATIC/SIPLUS image update, not by any OS patch you apply yourself — with_kb is 0 across the release, so every fix here arrives as vendor firmware or a Siemens security advisory, not a downloadable hotfix.
